Luma

Your words are the light.

Luma is named after the luminance channel, so hierarchy comes from lightness and almost never from hue. Messages you send are the inverse of the room around them: ink on a pale day, lit on a dark night. Everything else stays quiet.

The only color is a small amber lamp. It marks what needs your attention: unread messages and where you are. Someone who is online is lit too, with a thin halo in your own message color.

Design foundation for milestone 1. Every value on this page is read from design/tokens.json. Apple frames use Inter as a stand-in for SF Pro, and Windows uses Open Sans for Segoe UI Variable.

One identity, five native interfaces

Each platform keeps its own structure, navigation and type. They all share tokens, terms and behaviour.

Showing the default theme per frame

iOS and Android

iOS keeps a large display-face title, an inset search field and a compose button in the navigation bar. Android keeps the Material 3 structure, with a top app bar and an extended action button in Luma's inversion. Dynamic color is off, so the identity holds.

macOS

A three-column split view: sidebar, list and conversation. The toolbar is unified with the title bar. Keyboard first: ⌘N new chat, ⌘F search, ⌘1 to ⌘9 jump to a conversation.

Windows

A compact NavigationView rail with a list-detail layout. The backdrop is the ground tone, where Mica sits on Windows 11. Group chats show sender names and small avatars at the end of each run of messages.

Linux

Qt Quick with a custom Luma style, using the desktop's own UI font. Ctrl+K opens the quick switcher. Server-side window decorations are kept where the desktop provides them.

States

Cached content always renders first. The luma line under the header carries connection state, and the words under it say exactly what is happening.

Motion

Every animation explains a change. With reduced motion enabled, springs become short crossfades and the luma line holds still.

Message sentRises from the composer into place on the send spring, from 0.6 opacity.
Message receivedFades in over 160 ms. If you have scrolled up, the list stays put and a pill offers the new messages.
Receipt changesThe circle fills over 240 ms: dashed while pending, an outline once sent, half lit when delivered, fully lit when read.
ConnectionThe luma line breathes over 1.6 s while reconnecting and holds steady when offline. When connected, it is invisible.
TypingThree dots fade in turn, 160 ms apart. Nothing moves vertically.

Foundation

Contrast ratios are computed live from the tokens. Every text pairing meets WCAG AA in both themes.

Rules this page holds itself to

  • The lamp appears only on unread badges and the selection marker. It is never used for text. Presence is a luminance halo, never amber.
  • No gradients, glass, glow or decorative cards. Hairlines and tonal steps do the separating, and the one shadow belongs to floating surfaces.
  • The display face is for titles and empty states. Body text uses each platform's own UI font, and times use tabular figures.
  • Bubbles have no tails. A run of messages from one sender tightens its inner corners to 6 px.
